The twelve signal inputs and the sixteen Mix outputs carry whatever is patched into them, so they are given no family; only the two knob-value outputs are certain to be control voltages. Synth.notes: Read from src/Synth.cpp at the tag release/v2.1.1, commit f622217, which is the installed 2.1.1, alongside the README. The module is switched off entirely when the V/Oct input has no cable: Synth.cpp:912 takes the channel count from that jack alone and Synth.cpp:1300 writes 0V to both audio outputs and returns. The README's caveats are the other thing a new user needs: with no modulations assigned nothing is heard, because V/Oct reaches the oscillators only through an assignment and the amp is opened only by one. Ranges are left out of most lines on purpose: the modulatable parameters are configured through one helper (Synth.cpp:880) whose bounds change with the destination, and quoting a figure for the wrong one would be worse than quoting none. The assign buttons carry a description listing their destinations, which is what Rack shows on hover. The five Individual modulation outputs are polyphonic while the two audio outputs are not.

SplitStack.notes: Read from src/SplitStack.cpp at the tag release/v2.1.1, commit f622217, which is the installed 2.1.1. The README spells the section heading Spit/Stack. A part that is not playing has its outputs set to zero channels rather than to 0V (SplitStack.cpp:200 onwards), which is what makes a downstream synth go quiet rather than hold a note. The split test is strictly below the split point for part A and at or above it for part B (SplitStack.cpp:157). Learning the split point looks for the gate rising by more than 1V from its previous value (SplitStack.cpp:141), so a gate already high when the button is held does not set it.
